newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares seen ending week strong.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares seen ending week strong.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares are expected to end the week at new record levels as foreign and local buyers continue driving prices up, brokers said on Thursday.

The key industrial index rose 42.25 points on Thursday to close at a new all time high of 11,784.53 and brokers said it seemed headed to test the pyschologically important 12,000- barrier soon as buyers continued to chase prices up to generate volumes.

"There's potential for a further move up. The index may be heading for the 12,000-mark. There's not too many shares around and for buyers to see volumes they have to pay up. I expect the market to continue firm tomorrow," one broker said.

Among Thursday's winners, food group Natfoods surged 150 cents to 850, phamarceutical group Caps -- which raised its share earnings for the quarter ended June 30 -- leapt 100 cents to 3,800 as did International Holdings Limited to 2,400.
Bankers Barclays gained 20 cents to 3,350 and glass firm PGI put on 15 cents to 500.

A couple of counters bucked the trend, dragged lower by some profit-takers. These were merchant banker FMB which dropped 200 cents to 4,800 and household appliances-maker Capri which lost 30 cents to 500.
Minings were quiet with Wankie Colliery trading 25 cents up at 750. The mining index rose 9.35 points to 847.78.
